name: Universidade de Lisboa
englishBachelors: Four confirmed English degrees at ISEG; Técnico’s General Engineering has its own page. Design and Architecture need full-route language confirmation.
note: Formed by merging the classical and technical universities of Lisbon, and home to Instituto Superior Técnico.
summary: Public university in Lisbon with four confirmed English economics and business degrees at ISEG; Técnico’s General Engineering is listed separately.

ib.text: EU citizens apply through the national contest: IB final grade (on a 0–200 scale) 50%, IB exams replacing entrance exams 50%. ISEG's English degrees need Maths AA (SL/HL) or AI HL.

notes: The four degrees shown here are ISEG’s confirmed English routes. Each has a separate national-contest course from its Portuguese twin, with its own places and cut-off.

Técnico (IST), also part of ULisboa, has its own page here with its English-taught General Engineering degree. The three ULisboa–Shanghai University engineering routes select applicants in Shanghai, rather than through a Lisbon first-year application.

Language gap: ULisboa’s ‘Full Programmes’ page includes Design and Architecture, but their individual pages say PT/EN. These official pages do not confirm that every compulsory year can be completed in English for 2027. Ask the Lisbon School of Architecture before treating either as a complete English route.

The Arts and Humanities school states that teaching is Portuguese, with some English classes or classes switched to English. Its inclusion on ‘Full Programmes’ does not establish a complete English degree.

Faculty guidance explicitly places bachelor teaching in Portuguese at Sciences and Agriculture; ISCSP and Veterinary Medicine also state Portuguese teaching. Law and Fine Arts admissions require Portuguese. Human Kinetics’ language FAQ describes Portuguese classes with some English tutorials.

The individual ULisboa programme pages reviewed for Psychology, Education and Training, Nursing, Geography, Spatial Planning and Management, Dentistry, Medicine, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Veterinary Medicine and Fashion Design publish PT as the teaching language. A translated programme page or English assessment support is not a confirmed English degree.
